blocks.text: Nitrogen belongs to group 15 of the periodic table. In industry nitrogen is typically obtained by cooling air until it becomes a liquid; liquid nitrogen is commonly used for rapid cooling. In the laboratory nitrogen can be generated by slowly heating a solution of ammonium nitrite: NH4NO2(aq) gives N2(g) + 2H2O(l).

blocks.prompt: How is nitrogen isolated from air, and how is it made in the laboratory (exercise Q.2b)?
blocks.explanation: Industrially air is cooled and compressed until it liquefies, and nitrogen is separated from the liquid air (it boils off at -195.8 degrees C). In the laboratory a solution of ammonium nitrite is warmed gently; it decomposes to nitrogen gas and water.

items: Nitrogen: group 15, Z = 7, [He] 2s2 2p3, colourless gas, b.p. -195.8 degrees C; obtained by liquefying air, or in the lab by heating NH4NO2 to N2 + 2H2O.
